slides.text: The company that sells them fought to prove they're not chips. So, are they?

caption:
Pringles' maker once spent years arguing its own snack isn't a potato chip.

In Britain, most food has no VAT, a sales tax. Potato chips ("crisps" there) do. In 2008, Procter & Gamble said Pringles were too different to count: only about 40% potato, with a factory-made shape. A High Court judge agreed.

In 2009 the Court of Appeal reversed it, saying there was "more than enough potato." The company missed a refund of about £100 million (over $150 million).

So: chip or not?

Source: NBC News, Marketing Week, CMS Law
verification: High Court July 2008 sided with P&G; Court of Appeal 20 May 2009 reversed ('more than enough potato'); potato content about 40-42%; about £100m rebate at stake (NBC News, Marketing Week, CMS).
